subject: Data retention exception request - Acme (post-call recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps - data retention exception (Acme)

Hi Jordan / Samir,

Thanks again for the call earlier - appreciate the clear context on Acme's data handling needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of needs (from call):
- Zero/near-zero retention for request/response payloads that may contain PII.
- Shortened retention window for inference logs used for debugging/monitoring (you suggested 30 days).
- Data residency: all logs and stored embeddings to remain in us-east-1.
- Separate treatment for user profile PII (stored in your systems) vs transient inference payloads.

Proposed immediate next steps (from Redwood):
1) I’ll share a draft retention SLA and a short matrix of configurable retention profiles (attached).
2) Confirm which API routes/workloads you want configured to 0-retention vs shortened logs (please list the top 2-3 workloads).
3) I'll loop in Camila (security) and Rafael (solutions) to validate technical feasibility and timing.
4) Legal/Procurement: once we have the retention profile defined, we’ll produce an addendum / SOW redline and hand to your legal team for review.

Attachment: Data_Retention_SLA_draft.pdf (draft retention options + example wording)

Questions for you now:
- Can you confirm the 2-3 production routes that must be 0-retention?
- Is 30 days acceptable for audit/monitoring logs or do you need shorter?

I’ll wait for that list and then tag Camila/Rafael for the technical call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>, Legal Team <legal@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps - data retention exception (Acme)

Marissa - thanks for the summary and the draft. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Priority routes for 0-retention:
   - /v1/chat/completions (customer-facing chat service that surfaces PII in some cases)
   - /v1/embed (we send some user-identifiable metadata in embedding requests)

2) Desired retention windows:
   - Request/response payloads (raw): 0-retention if possible.
   - Inference logs (for troubleshooting/metrics): 30 days preferred, but we can consider 14 days if necessary.
   - Audit/security logs: 90 days on our end, but if Redwood stores copies we need 30 days.

3) Data residency: Must remain in us-east-1. No cross-region replication for logs/embeddings.

4) We will route contract redlines to our legal team. They may ask for an SLA clause that prohibits retention beyond the agreed windows and requires attestations.

We’d like Redwood to propose precise wording for 'zero-retention' and the operational controls you will enable to guarantee it (e.g., no persistent cache, KMS controls, no token logging). Also: what telemetry/usage metrics will Redwood retain for billing/diagnostics?

Samir and I are available for a 30-min call with Camila/Rafael next week if that helps.

Thanks - Jordan
Jordan Lee
Director, Platform Security | Acme Corp
jordan.lee@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps - data retention exception (Acme)

Jordan - great, this is very clear and helpful.

High-level response and proposed approach:
- Zero-retention: we can enable an "ephemeral mode" for specific routes where request/response payloads are not written to persistent storage. That will disable request/response logging and persistent KV cache for those routes. We’ll add a contractual SLA clause that Redwood will not persist raw payloads beyond the configured retention.
- Monitoring/metrics: Redwood will continue to collect aggregated telemetry for billing and platform health (request counts, latencies, error rates) but we can make that telemetry non-identifiable (no verbatim prompts) and retain aggregated metrics for 90 days by default.
- Inference/debug logs: we can set an account-level retention window (configurable per route). Proposed default for Acme: 14 days for inference/debug logs, 30 days for audit logs. If you need 30/90 we can negotiate.
- Data residency: we will pin your workload to us-east-1 and disable cross-region log replication for this account.

Attached is a slightly updated draft retention matrix (retention_matrix_acme.xlsx) and the SLA draft.

Next steps:
1) Camila/Rafael: can you confirm technical feasibility and any known trade-offs? Rafael - please include an ETA for implementing ephemeral-mode for the two listed routes (approx dev + rollout time).
2) Jordan: once Camila/Rafael confirm, I’ll produce suggested contract language for the addendum and loop legal.
3) If helpful, we can do a 30-min technical call next week (Camila / Rafael + Jordan / Samir).

If anything here needs to be stronger (e.g., explicit KMS key handling, HSM requirement), flag it and we’ll escalate with our security team.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior AE | Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps - data retention exception (Acme)

Marissa - thanks for pulling this together and Jordan for the clear asks. Quick internal notes / answers:

Feasibility summary (high-level):
- Ephemeral mode (0-retention) for specific routes: Supported. We have two levers:
  1) Disable persistent request/response logging for selected routes.
  2) Disable KV cache persistence (in-memory only) so nothing is written to disk.
  Both are deploy/config changes; low risk but will prevent us from replaying requests for deep debugging.

- Audit/log retention: We can enforce per-account/per-route retention windows and ensure logs remain in us-east-1 with no replication.

Trade-offs to call out for the customer:
- Zero-retention reduces our ability to debug customer-facing incidents; we’ll rely on aggregated metrics and sampling for debugging. Recommend keeping a brief 7-day short-term debugging window for non-PII logs where possible.
- Some platform features (e.g., long-term model quality regression analysis) may need opt-in if Acme chooses 0-retention for embedding storage.

Security controls to include in the addendum:
- Statement that raw request/response payloads for listed routes will not be persisted beyond the configured retention window.
- Confirmation that data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys (if requested) or Redwood-managed KMS by default.
- Assurance that logs/embeddings are pinned to us-east-1 and access is restricted.

ETA / implementation notes:
- Rafael: please confirm estimates, but ballpark 2 weeks to implement account-scoped ephemeral-mode and add per-route config + 1-week for QA and rollout.
- Legal: we will draft recommended SOW wording and add a short acceptance test for verifying ephemeral-mode during onboarding.

I’ll prepare suggested contract wording and a short redline for legal to review; Marissa - once Rafael confirms ETA I’ll send the redline.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Security Solutions | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
